//! Ground truth for the method-call rule, with rustc as the oracle.
//!
//! Every inherent and trait method returns its own callsign; every call
//! site is its own function, named for the grade the rule must assign it:
//! `c_p_*` proven, `c_m_*` modeled, `r_*` refused or declined (no edge).
//! `main` prints `<function>\t<callsign the call actually reached>`, so
//! the survey's edges can be checked against the compiler's own binding.
#![allow(dead_code, unused_variables, clippy::all)]

pub mod other;

pub struct Foo {
    pub bar: Bar,
    pub n: u32,
}
pub struct Bar;
pub struct Gen<T>(pub T);
pub struct Where;
pub type Alias = Foo;
#[cfg(unix)]
pub struct Amb {
    pub a: u8,
}
#[cfg(not(unix))]
pub struct Amb {
    pub b: u8,
}

/// Same name as `other::Holder`, a different field type: the one in this
/// file must never type a base written as `other::Holder`.
pub struct Holder<'a> {
    pub h: &'a Bar,
}

pub trait Tr {
    fn t(&self) -> &'static str;
    fn by_val(self) -> &'static str;
    fn only_trait(&self) -> &'static str;
}

/// Implemented for `&Foo`: rustc's first step on a `&&Foo` receiver is the
/// outer reference, where this impl outranks the inherent `Foo::d`.
pub trait Dr {
    fn d(&self) -> &'static str;
}

/// `Foo` here is the trait's type parameter, not the struct above: inside
/// the default body only the bound's `t` is visible.
pub trait Visit<Foo: Tr> {
    fn r_trait_generic(&self, n: &Foo) -> &'static str {
        n.t()
    }
}
pub struct V;
impl Visit<Foo> for V {}

impl Foo {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Foo { bar: Bar, n: 0 }
    }
    pub fn open() -> Result<Self, String> {
        Ok(Foo::new())
    }
    pub fn m(&self) -> &'static str {
        "Foo.m"
    }
    pub fn mm(&mut self) -> &'static str {
        "Foo.mm"
    }
    pub fn v(self) -> &'static str {
        "Foo.v"
    }
    pub fn g(&self) -> &Bar {
        &self.bar
    }
    pub fn t(&self) -> &'static str {
        "Foo.t"
    }
    pub fn by_val(&self) -> &'static str {
        "Foo.by_val"
    }
    pub fn clone(&self) -> &'static str {
        "Foo.clone"
    }
    pub fn d(&self) -> &'static str {
        "Foo.d"
    }
    pub fn c_m_self_field(&self) -> &'static str {
        self.bar.m()
    }
}

impl Dr for &Foo {
    fn d(&self) -> &'static str {
        "Foo@Dr.d"
    }
}

impl Tr for Foo {
    fn t(&self) -> &'static str {
        "Foo@Tr.t"
    }
    fn by_val(self) -> &'static str {
        "Foo@Tr.by_val"
    }
    fn only_trait(&self) -> &'static str {
        "Foo@Tr.only_trait"
    }
}

impl Bar {
    pub fn m(&self) -> &'static str {
        "Bar.m"
    }
}

impl<T> Gen<T> {
    pub fn m(&self) -> &'static str {
        "Gen.m"
    }
}

impl Where
where
    u8: Copy,
{
    pub fn m(&self) -> &'static str {
        "Where.m"
    }
}

impl Amb {
    pub fn m(&self) -> &'static str {
        "Amb.m"
    }
}

// Proven: a written receiver type whose form matches the inherent method's
// at the first lookup step, where rustc lets no trait outrank it.
fn c_p_ref(x: &Foo) -> &'static str {
    x.m()
}
fn c_p_refmut(x: &mut Foo) -> &'static str {
    x.mm()
}
fn c_p_val(x: Foo) -> &'static str {
    x.v()
}
fn c_p_let_ann() -> &'static str {
    let x: Foo = Foo::new();
    x.v()
}
fn c_p_trait_shadowed(x: &Foo) -> &'static str {
    x.t()
}
fn c_p_prelude_shadowed(x: &Foo) -> &'static str {
    x.clone()
}

// Modeled: a written type matched only at a later step with no visible
// candidate, or a type the file inferred.
fn c_m_autoref(x: Foo) -> &'static str {
    x.m()
}
fn c_m_field(x: &Foo) -> &'static str {
    x.bar.m()
}
fn c_m_ctor() -> &'static str {
    let x = Foo::new();
    x.m()
}
fn c_m_ctor_val() -> &'static str {
    Foo::new().v()
}
fn c_m_literal() -> &'static str {
    let x = Foo { bar: Bar, n: 1 };
    x.m()
}
fn c_m_chain(x: &Foo) -> &'static str {
    x.g().m()
}
fn c_m_try() -> Result<&'static str, String> {
    Ok(Foo::open()?.m())
}
fn c_m_unwrap() -> &'static str {
    Foo::open().unwrap().m()
}

// No edge: refused with a reason, or a receiver the file cannot type.
fn r_by_val_trait(x: Foo) -> &'static str {
    x.by_val()
}
fn r_prelude_later(x: Foo) -> &'static str {
    x.clone()
}
fn r_no_inherent(x: &Foo) -> &'static str {
    x.only_trait()
}
fn r_instantiated(x: &Gen<u8>) -> &'static str {
    x.m()
}
fn r_where(x: &Where) -> &'static str {
    x.m()
}
fn r_alias(x: &Alias) -> &'static str {
    x.m()
}
fn r_amb(x: &Amb) -> &'static str {
    x.m()
}
fn r_closure() -> &'static str {
    let f = |x: &Foo| x.m();
    f(&Foo::new())
}
fn r_for(v: Vec<Foo>) -> &'static str {
    for x in v {
        return x.m();
    }
    "none"
}
// A written type that is not the first lookup step: `&&Foo` probes the
// outer reference first, where `impl Dr for &Foo` wins.
fn r_double_ref(x: &&Foo) -> &'static str {
    x.d()
}
// A base written as `other::Holder`: this file's `Holder` must not type it.
fn r_foreign_field(x: &other::Holder) -> &'static str {
    x.h.m()
}

fn main() {
    let mut foo = Foo::new();
    #[cfg(unix)]
    let amb = Amb { a: 1 };
    #[cfg(not(unix))]
    let amb = Amb { b: 1 };
    let rows: Vec<(&str, &str)> = vec![
        ("c_p_ref", c_p_ref(&foo)),
        ("c_p_refmut", c_p_refmut(&mut foo)),
        ("c_p_val", c_p_val(Foo::new())),
        ("c_p_let_ann", c_p_let_ann()),
        ("c_p_trait_shadowed", c_p_trait_shadowed(&foo)),
        ("c_p_prelude_shadowed", c_p_prelude_shadowed(&foo)),
        ("c_m_autoref", c_m_autoref(Foo::new())),
        ("c_m_field", c_m_field(&foo)),
        ("Foo.c_m_self_field", foo.c_m_self_field()),
        ("c_m_ctor", c_m_ctor()),
        ("c_m_ctor_val", c_m_ctor_val()),
        ("c_m_literal", c_m_literal()),
        ("c_m_chain", c_m_chain(&foo)),
        ("c_m_try", c_m_try().unwrap()),
        ("c_m_unwrap", c_m_unwrap()),
        ("r_by_val_trait", r_by_val_trait(Foo::new())),
        ("r_prelude_later", r_prelude_later(Foo::new())),
        ("r_no_inherent", r_no_inherent(&foo)),
        ("r_instantiated", r_instantiated(&Gen(1u8))),
        ("r_where", r_where(&Where)),
        ("r_alias", r_alias(&foo)),
        ("r_amb", r_amb(&amb)),
        ("r_closure", r_closure()),
        ("r_for", r_for(vec![Foo::new()])),
        ("Visit.r_trait_generic", V.r_trait_generic(&foo)),
        ("r_double_ref", r_double_ref(&&foo)),
        (
            "r_foreign_field",
            r_foreign_field(&other::Holder { h: &other::Qux }),
        ),
    ];
    for (name, reached) in rows {
        println!("{name}\t{reached}");
    }
}
